# Kyoto Trip Plan: 5 Days, 2 Adults, USD 1,800 Budget

A compact Kyoto plan centered on temples, food markets, and one easy hike, with lodging in transit-friendly central areas. Costs below are estimated for 2 adults and exclude international flights.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Cost Plan

### Day 1: Arrival, Gion, and Higashiyama
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, and settle near a central station area.
- Afternoon: Walk Yasaka Shrine, Maruyama Park, and the preserved lanes around Gion and Sannenzaka.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f8/A199_Japan_Kyoto_Maruyama_Park_Gion_Ar%C3%A9a_%284764445344%29.jpg Alt=Afternoon: Walk Yasaka Shrine, Maruyama Park, and the preserved lanes around Gion and Sannenzaka, Kyoto, Japan
- Dinner: Kaiseki-lite or a casual set meal in Gion or Pontocho.
- Estimated cost: Lodging USD 140; food USD 70; transit/entry USD 15; total USD 225.

### Day 2: Southern Kyoto Temples and Nishiki Market
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Fushimi Inari Taisha early for quieter trails and shrine gates.
- Afternoon: Nishiki Market for lunch and snack hopping, then Kiyomizu-dera and nearby temple streets.
Media: Alt=Afternoon: Nishiki Market for lunch and snack hopping, then Kiyomizu-dera and nearby temple streets, Kyoto, Japan
- Dinner: Izakaya or tofu-focused dinner in central Kyoto.
- Estimated cost: Lodging USD 140; food USD 80; transit/entry USD 20; total USD 240.

### Day 3: Arashiyama Easy Hike and Riverside Area
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Easy hike on the Arashiyama Bamboo Grove, river paths, and the hills around Iwatayama Monkey Park if you want a light climb.
- Afternoon: Tenryu-ji, Togetsukyo Bridge, and slow time by the river.
- Dinner: Tempura, soba, or a relaxed riverside meal.
- Estimated cost: Lodging USD 140; food USD 75; transit/entry USD 25; total USD 240.

### Day 4: Northern Kyoto Temples and Garden Time
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- Morning: Kinkaku-ji, then Ryoan-ji for the rock garden.
- Afternoon: Daitoku-ji area or Nijo Castle depending on pace and interest.
- Dinner: Kyoto-style obanzai or a ramen spot near downtown.
- Estimated cost: Lodging USD 140; food USD 75; transit/entry USD 25; total USD 240.

### Day 5: Market Morning and Departure Buffer
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- Morning: Slow breakfast, final shopping, or a return visit to Nishiki Market for gifts and snacks.
- Afternoon: Leave room for airport transfer or a final temple stop near your hotel.
- Dinner: If staying the night, choose a last Kyoto dinner near Kyoto Station or Shijo.
- Estimated cost: Lodging USD 140; food USD 55; transit/entry USD 20; total USD 215.

## Best Kyoto Neighborhoods for Central Lodging

### 1) Kyoto Station Area
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- Best for: easiest transit, airport access, day trips, and practical hotel choices.
- Why it works: direct rail/subway/bus connections and simple luggage handling.
- Trade-off: less atmospheric than Gion or Kawaramachi.

### 2) Kawaramachi / Shijo / Downtown
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg
- Best for: food, nightlife, shopping, and strong bus/subway access.
- Why it works: closest all-around base for Nishiki Market, Gion, and many dinner options.
- Trade-off: busier and slightly pricier than station-area stays.

### 3) Gion / Higashiyama Edge
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Best for: temple atmosphere, early morning walks, and classic Kyoto scenery.
- Why it works: ideal if you want to step out into scenic streets and reach eastern temples quickly.
- Trade-off: fewer large-value hotel choices and can be quieter at night.

### 4) Karasuma Oike
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg
- Best for: a balanced central base with good subway access and calmer streets.
- Why it works: excellent for moving around the city with less crowding than the core shopping districts.
- Trade-off: fewer dining options right outside the door than Shijo/Kawaramachi.

## Budget Fit and Lodging Recommendation

| Category | Estimated Total for 5 Days |
|---|---:|
| Lodging | USD 700 |
| Food | USD 355 |
| Local transit | USD 70 |
| Temple/attraction entry | USD 70 |
| Snacks, coffee, buffer | USD 120 |
| Total | **USD 1,315** |

- Your **USD 1,800** budget is comfortable for this plan.
- Recommended lodging target: **USD 120–170 per night for a well-located 2-adult room**.
- Best overall base: **Shijo/Kawaramachi** if you want food and transit balance, or **Kyoto Station** if convenience matters most.
